title: A finitely generated field extension becomes separable after finite purely inseparable extensions
statement: Let $K/k$ be a finitely generated field extension [def-pc-field-extension] (i.e. $K=k(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ for finitely many $a_1,\dots,a_n\in K$). Then there exist a field $K'$ with a field homomorphism $K\to K'$, and a subfield $k'\subseteq K'$ containing the image of $k$ under $k\to K\to K'$, such that $k'/k$ is a finite purely inseparable extension and $K'/K$ is a finite purely inseparable extension [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], and $K'/k'$ is a separable field extension in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. In other words there is a commutative square of field extensions $k\to k'\to K'$, $k\to K\to K'$ with $k'/k$, $K'/K$ finite purely inseparable and $K'/k'$ separable.
